records.question: Which warehouses are underused, below the level that triggers a closure review?
records.expected_answer: Hat Yai (64%) and Da Nang (62%) are below 65%. Note the watch list needs two consecutive quarters below 65%; the report only gives an annual figure.

answer.answer: None of the listed facilities fall below the 65% threshold. The document states that sites below 65% utilisation for two consecutive quarters are placed on a 'consolidation watch list' (not a closure review). The lowest utilisation among the 23 major facilities is Da Nang at 62%, which is below 65%; Hat Yai is 64%, also below 65%. No other listed facility is below 65%. Note: this list covers only the 23 major facilities; smaller satellite sites are not listed.

citations.quote: Sites that remain below 65% for two consecutive quarters are placed on a consolidation watch list

answer.judge_reason: The answer correctly identifies Hat Yai (64%) and Da Nang (62%) as below 65% and notes the two-consecutive-quarters rule, but it contradicts itself by first claiming no facilities fall below the threshold.

records.question: Why did service quality slip toward the end of the year?
records.expected_answer: Flooding in southern Thailand closed sections of the main southern highway; line-haul to Hat Yai was rerouted over slower roads

answer.answer: Full-year OTD was 94.0%, but performance dipped in the fourth quarter because severe flooding in southern Thailand closed sections of the main southern highway for several weeks, forcing line-haul traffic to Hat Yai to be rerouted through slower inland roads. Service recovered in December once the highway reopened.

citations.quote: Flooding in southern Thailand closed sections of the main southern highway, and line-haul to Hat Yai was rerouted through slower inland roads.
Service recovered in December once the highway reopened.

answer.judge_reason: Matches the reference: flooding in southern Thailand closed the main southern highway, forcing rerouted, slower line-haul to Hat Yai.
